Phase 4 acceptance evidence — four microservices + end-to-end routing
Generated: 2026-07-31 07:02:04 UTC
Go: go version go1.26.5 darwin/arm64
Postgres: 16.14

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Phase 4):
  'each service has integration tests against a real (test-container or
   docker-compose) Postgres instance — not mocks for the DB layer.'
  'Gateway can route to all four through Phase 3's middleware chain
   end-to-end.'

=== per-service databases (no shared tables, plan 1.3) ===
  ecom
  ecom_auth
  ecom_catalog
  ecom_orders
  ecom_payment

=== INTEGRATION TESTS against real Postgres (-race) ===
  auth:     ok  	services/auth	2.526s
  catalog:  ok  	services/catalog	2.385s
  orders:   ok  	services/orders	2.029s
  payment:  ok  	services/payment	1.996s

=== END-TO-END through the gateway ===
-- 1. signup on a public route, no token required --
   201, JWT issued by auth and accepted by the gateway

-- 2. protected routes reject anonymous requests --
   /catalog/products    -> 401
   /orders/             -> 401
   /payment/charges     -> 401

-- 3. authenticated cross-service checkout --
   catalog: product created, stock=10
   orders:  order c939e77d status=pending total=5000 (priced by catalog, not the client)
   catalog: stock=10 reserved=2 available=8 (stock held for the pending order)
   payment: 5e1b0685 status=succeeded
   payment: redelivered charge returned 5e1b0685 — same id, exactly one charge

-- 4. declined charge is a recorded outcome, not a lost request --
   status=failed reason=card declined

-- 5. one correlation ID spans the gateway and the services --
   client sent X-Correlation-ID: evidence-trace-1785481338
   orders log: msg='order created' correlation_id=evidence-trace-1785481338
   This is the Phase 6 capability: one ID reconstructs a request's path.
